reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker presents Forsage as a paid slot-based project requiring 0.05 ETH, where inviting and placing partners generates payout flows to a participant’s Ethereum wallet. It promotes substantial conditional earnings, including hundreds of ETH and lifelong passive income, while noting that these outcomes are not established as having occurred or being attainable.

citations.quote: I'm bringing into your attention guys the first in history absolutely decentralized matrix project that is called Forsage.
It's recommended to start with at least three slots in each platform x3 and x4. Total 0.35 Ethereum
turn on the money machine and earn a lot of the theory M
So, to register in Forsage, You need 0.05 ETH.
All the rest of the slots you can purchase separately in order from the smallest to the largest.

opening.argument: Judge, the earnings example should be read as conditional, not as a report that viewers have earned those sums. It begins with an assumption about continuing to open slots, and its dollar comparison depends on a stated Ethereum price. More importantly, the explanation identifies a condition under which payments go to an upline instead of the participant. Those qualifications do not prove Forsage is sound, but they matter when deciding whether this is an unconditional promise rather than an explanation of how the described system would operate.

citations.quote: If you continue opening up each week a new slot, you'll be able to generate as much as 613,35 Ethereum on Forsage X3 and 817 ETH on Forsage X4
now if ethereum is 250 dollars that is over three hundred and fifty thousand dollars
If the member, he doesn't have the next slot open to him after the second reinvestment, all payments will be sent to the upline.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to the registration cost, additional slot purchases and the phrase “money machine.” Those establish an enthusiastic, paid presentation, but not that the projected earnings actually occurred or were promised irrespective of participation. The speaker also explains that continued payments can depend on an upgrade—a material limitation that the prosecution’s selected quotations leave out.

citations.quote: So, to register in Forsage, You need 0.05 ETH.
To get the payments after reinvestment, you need to do an upgrade.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional arithmetic is not a meaningful risk warning here. The video urges viewers to start with paid slots, presents very large earnings as attainable and says activated slots will bring lifelong passive income. Its upgrade condition reinforces the concern: receiving further payments is tied to another purchase. The defense’s quotations qualify the pitch; they do not turn it into a neutral discussion of risk.

citations.quote: It's recommended to start with at least three slots in each platform x3 and x4. Total 0.35 Ethereum
all slots are activated and will bring you income for life passive income for life
To get the payments after reinvestment, you need to do an upgrade.

opening.argument: Judge, consider how much of this presentation is devoted to explaining mechanics. It distinguishes the layouts of X3 and X4, describes where a participant is placed, and walks through what happens when a slot fills and reinvests. That is operational instruction a viewer could assess without accepting the speaker’s earnings claims. The paid registration mentioned by the prosecution is part of the mechanism being explained; by itself, it does not settle whether the video’s central function is instruction or solicitation.

citations.quote: On Forsage 3, you have 1 line with 3 spots.
2 lines with 4 spots. Two spots in line 1 and four spots in line 2.
As soon as the last spot is filled the current slots closes and goes to archive

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker names a price and discusses purchases. But those details also make the operational account intelligible: the video explains that slots have different prices and that a filled slot reinvests. Quoting the entry cost and the largest earnings language without that intervening explanation risks treating every demonstration of a paid system as nothing more than an instruction to join it.

citations.quote: each of the slots is twice as Expensive as the previous
Reinvestment goes automatically.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanics are precisely what make this a promotional recruitment pitch rather than detached technical teaching. The explanation says invited partners take places below the participant and that a partner’s slot purchase goes directly to the participant’s wallet. It then recommends buying multiple slots and urges viewers to earn. Diagramming the matrix does not remove the solicitation embedded in the explanation.

citations.quote: When you invite partners, they take places below you.
his purchase of the slot 100% of it goes directly to your personal Ethereum wallet
It's recommended to start with at least three slots in each platform x3 and x4. Total 0.35 Ethereum

opening.argument: Judge, the described purchase is a priced slot in a stated system, not a request in the cited material to surrender account credentials or send funds to an undisclosed operator. The speaker says additional slots can be bought separately, explains that payments go to participants’ wallets, and contrasts that arrangement with funds held centrally. One need not certify the service as safe to recognize the narrower point: the evidence describes participant-to-participant transactions with disclosed slot and upgrade rules, rather than establishing theft through a hidden custodian.

citations.quote: All the rest of the slots you can purchase separately in order from the smallest to the largest.
Each payment goes directly to the wallet of one of the participants.
the funds are being stored in a centralized location.
To get the payments after reinvestment, you need to do an upgrade.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s 0.05 ETH entry price and separately purchasable slots show what is being sold, not an undisclosed taking of funds. Its wallet-payment point likewise cuts both ways: the speaker says payments go directly to participants, rather than claiming that an operator holds the money and will later release returns. The strongest criticism may be of the economics of those transactions, but that is more specific than the opening’s implication that a paid entry price alone resolves the case.

citations.quote: So, to register in Forsage, You need 0.05 ETH.
Each payment goes directly to the wallet of one of the participants.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A hidden custodian or credential request is not required for the concern shown here. The speaker expressly links inviting partners to positions beneath the viewer, links a partner’s purchase to a payment into the viewer’s wallet, and says an upgrade is needed to receive payments after reinvestment. Direct wallet transfers do not make that paid, recruitment-driven structure ordinary commerce.
